chunks: And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal, from Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.الْمُفَضَّلُ: Al-Mufaddal, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.زَيْدٌ: Zayd, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Amr ibn Uthman, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Like it' (mithluhu) signify in Shia hadith chains regarding legal rulings?
ai.summary: This is a concise hadith from the chapter of Confession in Illness in Tahdhib al-Ahkam. The phrase 'Like it' indicates that the ruling or narration previously cited in the sequence applies here as well, typically referring to the validity of confession in illness. It is transmitted through a chain involving Al-Mufaddal and Zayd, reflecting the rigorous isnad verification characteristic of Shaykh al-Tusi's work in establishing legal precedents for end-of-life declarations.
